title: Fix hibernation failure due to swap location
summary: If hibernation fails with 'No such file or directory', it is often because the swap file is in a protected directory like /home. Move the swap file to a supported location.

steps.explain: Disable the problematic swap file. Replace <SWAP_PATH> with the path to your swap file (e.g., /home/user/swap).

placeholders.name: SWAP_PATH
placeholders.description: Path to the swap file causing the error

steps.explain: Delete the swap file from the protected directory.

placeholders.name: SWAP_PATH
placeholders.description: Path to the swap file causing the error

steps.explain: Create a new swap file in a supported location (e.g., /swapfile) and update your fstab or swap unit configuration.

rollback.explain: Recreate the swap file in the original location if needed, though this is not recommended.

warnings: Deleting a swap file will cause the system to lose that swap space. Ensure you have another swap space configured before proceeding.
